title: Thought Record Completion Lag After Trigger
dataSources: Mood entries (`daylio:entry`), CBT thought records (`cbt:record`), breathwork sessions (`breathwork:session`), and therapy homework items (`therapy:homework`).
app: Wellbeing journaling telemetry from Daylio exports, CBT thought records, breathwork apps, and therapy homework trackers sent to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=cbt:record
| search completion_delay_min=*
| stats avg(completion_delay_min) as avg_completion_delay_min perc90(completion_delay_min) as p90_completion_delay_min count as samples by trigger_type
| sort 0 - avg_completion_delay_min
description: Measures CBT thought-record completion lag by trigger type.
value: Completion lag shows whether the thought-record habit is being used while the event is still fresh enough to help.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for CBT thought-record completion lag to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 CBT thought-record completion lag.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights how long CBT thought-record completion lag usually takes, so slowdowns are obvious instead of anecdotal.
